name: v1.23.0
body:
## Install

```bash
npm i @opengsd/gsd-core@1.23.0
# or
npm i @opengsd/gsd-core@latest
```

## What's Changed

### Added

- **Run a plan on another runtime** — a plan that declares `executor_runtime` is executed by that runtime's own CLI in a GSD-created worktree when `workflow.cross_runtime_execution` is on, and falls back to the host's dispatch with one reason whenever the target cannot run (#6303). (#6350)
- **Capabilities can now guide external code reviewers** — a new `review:pre` loop point lets an enabled capability add `reviewer`-targeted guidance to the single prompt `/gsd-review` (and every `/gsd-plan-review-convergence` cycle) sends to external reviewer lanes, so reviews are judged under the same project guidance as planning. With no such capability the prompt is unchanged; the install summary now names this cross-reviewer egress. (#6492) (#6492)
- **Deep verification before UAT** — set `workflow.deep_verify` and `/gsd-verify-work` first has an agent enumerate interaction-level behaviors from the plan, summary and changed files, run each one it can through a browser MCP server, and leave you only judgment items, failed behaviors and anything it could not run; `workflow.deep_verify_all_phases` widens it beyond UI phases (#3858). (#6378)
- **Plan-review convergence can run unattended** — `/gsd-plan-review-convergence --on-escalation exit` ends a non-converged run with a `CONVERGENCE_STATUS` line (`converged`, `open_conflicts`, `stalled`, `max_cycles`) instead of asking, and `/gsd-review --cycle-summary` returns the `CYCLE_SUMMARY` counters on its own, so a caller with no person attached no longer re-implements the counting rules. (#4617) (#6493)
- **`gsd-tools project-context` reports how it found the git layout, and most commands no longer start `git` to find the project** — `provenance.layout` is `filesystem` when the checkout, the main checkout and the shared git dir were read from `.git`, `gitdir` and `commondir`, and `git` when `git rev-parse` was asked. A plain checkout, a linked worktree of a non-bare repository and a directory outside any repository are now read from the filesystem, which removes one `git` process (two in a linked worktree) from every `gsd-tools` call there. (#6355) (#6372)

### Changed

- **Config resolution now exposes per-key provenance and honors section barriers** — a new read-only owner reports the producing layer for project and runtime-setting values, while the assembled loader no longer recreates lower/default projections beneath an explicitly non-object section. Init/docs payloads make only absent flags explicit as false and use the manifest timeout default; configured non-boolean values retain their prior representation. An object section in the workstream config overrides a non-object section in the root config, as the assembled loader merges them. A null workflow disables inherited quality gates and a null review removes default prompt trimming. The default-on planner watchdog remains the documented fail-safe exception. (#6497)
- **`/gsd-plan-phase` now validates each `<automated>` command without running it** — a stated `<fails_when>` cannot reveal that a command does not parse, so a plan could pass every check and still ship commands that could not run (`Msg 8155`, a one-argument `CONCAT()`). Where a validate-only mode exists (`bash -n`, `node --check`, `ast.parse`, `SET PARSEONLY ON`, `cargo metadata --no-deps`), the planner runs it and records `[VALIDATED: …]` or `[UNVALIDATABLE: <reason>]` in the task's `<verify>`; plan-checker check 8g warns on a command with no record. Forms that look like validators but execute or write (`py_compile`, `cargo check`, `npm run --dry-run`, `terraform validate`) are named and banned. (#4586) (#6484)
- **`worktree base-check` now reports which settings layer supplied `worktree.baseRef`** — `resolveEffectiveBaseRef` reads the value through the family-B config resolver and returns its producing layer, and the base-check result carries it as `baseRefLayer` (`runtime-local`, `runtime-shared`, `runtime-user`, or `null`). Verdicts are unchanged: `head` from any layer is trusted under the harness as #4588 measured, and a settings layer whose `baseRef` is not a string is still skipped. (#6031) (#6529)
- **`query dispatch-isolation` answers `none` while it holds a sequential degrade an earlier dispatch step recorded** — for up to ten minutes after a step records `none` with `--force-isolation`, a plain query whose `--phase` and `--plan`, where it passes non-empty ones, equal the record's prints `none`, not the runtime's isolation capability. Under `--json` it marks that answer `held: true` with `decidedAt`, when the held decision was made; a query that is not holding gives `held: false`, and so does `inspect-dispatch-isolation`, which is never held. The ten minutes run from when the degrade was decided: a dispatch step that follows a held `none` re-records it with the new `--renew-held <decidedAt>` option, which does not extend the hold. A step that decides a sequential degrade itself (an `execute-plan` Pattern B segment run, the gate's orchestrator-worktree fallback) records a new `none` with its own ten minutes, so such steps run less than ten minutes apart keep a query that names no phase or plan answering `none`. A query that holds writes no decision, but it records the executor identity it derives for its own phase or plan under `.gsd/dispatch-isolation-identity/`, which the isolation guards read with the other records, so the agents that plans' `agent_hint`s route to are classified as current as after a query that records a decision; a query that cannot write that record still holds and records no decision, and while that `none` can be held the guards treat every valid non-role agent as an executor where something stops the write (an unsafe phase or plan, a directory at the record name, an identity or `.gsd` directory the process cannot write and search, a linked `.gsd/.gitignore`). The isolation sentinel gains a `decided_by` field (`caller` or `resolver`) naming who recorded the decision and a `decided_at` field recording when. **This changes the output contract of `query dispatch-isolation`:** during a hold its stdout and its `--json` `isolation` report `none` and its `harnessFlag` and `exec` are cleared, so a script that reads them as the runtime's capability should read `inspect-dispatch-isolation` instead. A plan that declares `executor_runtime` (#6303) and is dispatched to that runtime keeps that answer during a hold, `held: true` beside it, and the held query records no decision. (#4904) (#6494)

### Fixed

- **The audit-uat scope text names the archived phases it scans** — the skill and command declared only the live `phases/` globs, so an operator read the audit as live-phases-only while it also walks the milestone archives (flat `v*-phases` and `ws-*` shapes) under the active scope's root and under every workstream; both scope blocks now name them, and a test seeds every layout and fails if the scan reaches one the text does not name. (#6232) (#6450)
- **`state begin-phase --plans N` refuses instead of silently dropping the count** — on a STATE.md with no `Total Plans in Phase:` field and no `Plan:` line in `## Current Position`, the command wrote Status and Last Activity, recorded no plan count and exited 0, so the caller believed the count had landed (the frontmatter kept `total_plans: 0`); it now exits non-zero with the typed reason `plans_no_line` before any write, and behaves as before when either place can hold the count or `--plans` is not given. (#6399) (#6516)
- **plan-phase records the phase name and plan count in STATE.md** — step 13b passed `--name "${PHASE_NAME}"` and `--plans "${PLAN_COUNT}"` to `state planned-phase` with neither variable ever set (each workflow fence is its own shell), so STATE.md recorded no phase name; the step now assigns the phase number placeholder, reads the curated display name from `roadmap.get-phase` and the plan count from `find-phase` (both workstream-scoped), and stops when the plan count cannot be read. (#6257) (#6471)
- **Plan-review convergence records the live plan count in STATE.md** — the converged step passed the physical count taken before the loop, which counted superseded plans and missed plans added or removed during convergence. It now re-reads the live (non-superseded) count right before `state planned-phase`; the initial planning check keeps the physical count. (#6122) (#6406)
- **The code-review disposition ledger no longer loses recorded decisions without saying so** — a decision displaced by a reused finding id is now reported on the console on every path (including a fix report that decides the new finding), a review heading with a review-scoped prefix such as `### W6-CR-01:` is counted and named instead of recording nothing, a ledger row outside the id grammar is named and kept verbatim instead of deleted on rewrite, and an unrecognised frontmatter id no longer lets the next title overwrite another finding's. (#5802) (#6461)
- **Hermes dispatch calls now deliver the role prompt as the task's `context`** — the installed workflows named `gsd_role` and `gsd_role_prompt`, which Hermes's `delegate_task` does not accept, and never said where the role prompt goes, so orchestrators told the child to read the role file as tool output (windowed, truncated, compacted) and the child lost the plan; each call now carries only `goal`, `context` and `role`, with the role prompt's full contents in `context` and the plan as the child's own first read. (#6066) (#6379)
- **`~/.gsd/defaults.json` now merges per key inside a project** — a global default such as `model_profile` or `effort.agent_overrides` is honored whenever the project config does not set that key, instead of being dropped for the whole project because a `.planning/config.json` exists. A key the project sets still wins, a present non-object project section still blocks the global value, and the install-stamped `runtime` never fills in. `config-get`, capability gates, the omit gate, the install-time effort/model/tool merges and several single-file readers now resolve through one owner, so a value set in the root config or the global defaults is no longer ignored by a reader that looked at one file. The "global keys are ignored for model resolution" warning is removed because no listed key is inert any more. (#6540)
- **Requirement IDs shared by plans of one parallel worktree wave are now marked complete after the wave merges** — each worktree executor's shared-ID gate sees only its own `SUMMARY.md`, so an ID declared by two or more plans was blocked in every executor and none marked it (it stayed unchecked until phase completion, or forever if the ROADMAP requirements line did not cite it); the orchestrator's post-wave step now evaluates the gate once on the merged tree, marks the IDs whose declaring plans all have summaries (only when the post-merge tests passed), and commits REQUIREMENTS.md. (#6102) (#6393)
- **`roadmap upgrade` rollback no longer overwrites a file another writer changed** — when a migration failed, rollback restored every snapshot unconditionally, silently destroying an edit another writer saved to ROADMAP.md, STATE.md, PROJECT.md, config.json or a rewritten phase file in the meantime; it now restores a file only while it still holds what the migration wrote, leaves any other file as found, and names each one in the failure message. A file the migration created is removed only if it still holds what the migration wrote. (#6351) (#6473)
- **Budget `low` routes every tier to the provider's cheapest model** — the `anthropic` and `anthropic-fable` presets sent opus-tier agents (the quality-profile planner and executor) to `claude-opus-4-5`, which collapses to the current Opus on Claude, under the budget the settings table documents as haiku in every column. The opus `low` cell is now `claude-haiku-4-5` in both presets, and the same disagreement is fixed for `openai` (`gpt-5.6-luna`) and `qwen` (`qwen3-coder-next`). A test now fails when a preset's `low` cells differ from the documented table row. (#6125) (#6410)
- **Codex update no longer aborts on current agent settings or moves nested feature settings** — a bare `[agents]` table holding `enabled`, `max_concurrent_threads_per_session`, `default_subagent_model` or `default_subagent_reasoning_effort` now passes the post-write schema check and is kept through an install, and dotted assignments such as `multi_agent_v2.<key> = …` under `[features]` stay in `[features]` instead of being relocated into the table above it. (#6165) (#6429)
- **Codex install writes one agent `.toml` per role from the canonical source** — the Codex emit no longer renders the `gsd-*.compact.md` alternates, which share their canonical sibling's role name and silently overwrote it in directory order, the install reports the real role count instead of one inflated by 29, and two sources naming one role now fail the install instead of one replacing the other. (#6158) (#6426)
- **The Bash guard denies `claude --agent {gsd-debugger,x}` and its brace-expanded spellings** — the debugger-spawn check judged the `--agent` value as written, so bash brace expansion (`{gsd-debugger,x}`, `gsd-{debugger,x}`, `--agent={x,gsd-debugger}`, a plugin-namespaced alternative) hid a `gsd-debugger` launch and the command was allowed; the value is now judged by every alternative it expands to, a quoted word is judged as written, and brace lists that only name other agents stay allowed. (#6439) (#6496)
- **The secret-read guard denies a read nested past the nesting limit instead of allowing it unscanned** — `cat .env` inside four `bash -c` layers (or five nested `"$( )"`, backticks, process substitutions, `eval`, `xargs` or `git -c` scripts) was allowed because the guard stopped rescanning at three levels, while three layers were blocked. A command nested deeper than three levels is now blocked with the named code `nesting-too-deep`, the way an over-length command is blocked as `command-too-large`; a secret read found at a shallower level is still the block reported. The guard also now descends into backticks nested with escaped backticks (`` `echo \`cat .env\`` ``), which it used to end at the first escaped backtick and read as plain text. (#6136) (#6412)
- **A closed deferred item with a `### Resolution` heading is one closed item** — the deferred-items reader treated any heading followed by a deeper heading as a container, so an item written as a titled heading with body bullets and a Resolution child was reported as one open item per bullet and the audit could not be cleared; a heading whose deeper headings only record its closure is now the entry itself, closed by that resolution. (#6239) (#6454)
- **The gate evaluation-scope resolver reads signed commits whatever `log.showSignature` says** — with the setting on, a signed commit's `gpg:` lines landed before its record in the resolver's `git log` output, so the log parser dropped the commit silently (a gate's scope narrowed or came back empty) and a `git show --name-only` listed the `gpg:` text as file names; every `git log` and `git show` whose output the resolver parses now states `--no-show-signature`. (#6272) (#6526)
- **The PATH-export and canonical-path hooks now treat two letter-case spellings of one folder as the same path on macOS** — they compared `fs.realpathSync` results, which keep the caller's letter case on a case-insensitive volume, so one install reached through two spellings wrote two `export PATH=` lines and the plugin bundle self-heal rejected a bundle that was inside the root (and a correct link could read as wrong); both hooks now resolve with `realpathSync.native` on both sides of every comparison, and the symlink-escape checks are unchanged. (#6107) (#6395)
- **`/gsd-code-review --files` reviews exactly the listed files on macOS and zsh, and fails closed** — the comma split used bash-only `read -a` in a different block from the one that used it (zsh: `bad option: -a`, so the list was empty), the repository check used GNU `realpath -m` (BSD: every relative path looked outside), and a list that resolved to nothing silently widened to the phase scope while still logging `--files override`. The split now lives in the same block with a portable loop, paths resolve through `node`, and a list that resolves to no reviewable file inside the repository prints an error and exits non-zero. The reviewer-lane slug list splits portably too, and the macOS note no longer sends users to install coreutils. (#6152) (#6417)
- **The executor no longer grants itself a `git reset --hard` exception at startup** — its list of commands prohibited inside a worktree exempted the `<worktree_branch_check>` step, which has been verify-only since #48: on a failed assertion it exits 42 and the orchestrator recovers. The prohibition is now unconditional, matching the branch-check fragment. The git-integration reference that execute-plan hands the executor as required reading no longer lists `git reset --hard` as a failure-recovery option either. (#5416)
- **The executor path guard runs under zsh and gives the same verdicts as under bash** — the guard that parallel executors run before an `<automated>` command used bash-only `read -ra` and a 0-based array pop in its path normalizer, and `${s:i:1}` substrings that zsh reads as a history modifier, so under zsh every command errored and no cwd drift or main-checkout path was ever reported. The normalizer is now plain string handling, the substrings use `${s:$i:1}`, and a path that normalizes to the filesystem root is `/` rather than `//`. (#6153) (#6424)
- **`/gsd-health` reports W032 when the gsd-core Claude Code plugin is enabled but no statusline feeds the context monitor** — the plugin registers `gsd-context-monitor.js` but not `gsd-statusline.js`, the only writer of the bridge file the monitor reads, so a plugin-only install silently never shows the 35% and 25% remaining context warnings (and the opt-in hooks the npm installer registers are inactive too); the new advisory W032 names the cause and the fix (the npm installer), and an npm install, a disabled plugin or another runtime reports nothing. (#6430) (#6476)
- **`init` and `agent-skills` no longer crash under a runtime id GSD does not resolve** — since 1.16.0 every `init` command exited 1 with `UnknownRuntimeError` (and `agent-skills` too, even with no skills configured) on any host whose runtime id is not first-party, such as an out-of-tree host plugin, so GSD could not start there; the agents check now reports `agents_installed: null` with `agents_check_reason: "unknown_runtime"` instead of throwing, `agent-skills` resolves its skills location only when there are skill entries, the W010 health rule and the new-project and new-milestone warnings treat `null` as not-checkable, and installing under an unknown id still refuses. (#5236) (#6458)
- **A ROADMAP heading that only mentions a milestone's version no longer becomes that milestone's heading** — `## Carried forward to v0.5.0 (inputs, not phases)` was selected as the v0.5.0 heading, so every STATE.md write replaced the curated `milestone_name` with `(inputs, not phases)`, even when the real `## v0.5.0 Search Revamp` heading came later. A heading now counts as a version's milestone heading only when the version token leads its text (only ✅ 📋 🚧, bold markers and the word `Milestone` may precede it), and selection and section detection read that one rule, so a mention heading is neither selected, counted as a section, nor the end of the previous milestone's window. (#6149) (#6416)
- **`/gsd-phase --insert` records the typed description in the roadmap-evolution note without running it** — the state-update step passed the description to `state.add-roadmap-evolution --note` as model-filled text inside shell double quotes, so `$(...)`, backticks or a stray `"` in a description were executed or broke the command after the insert had already run; the step now takes the description and after-phase from the typed arguments and passes them as variables, and both state verbs forward `--ws` (it was unset in those fences). (#6195) (#6491)
- **A subagent no longer gets the parent session's context warning as its own** — in Claude Code a subagent's hook input carries the parent's `session_id`, so the context monitor read the parent's usage and told the subagent `CONTEXT WARNING: Usage at N%` with the parent's N, and could spend the parent's debounce or start its CRITICAL `record-session` write. An input with `agent_id` now exits before touching any of the session's monitor files; this holds on every event, so a subagent's PreCompact no longer clears the parent's bridge and its Stop, SubagentStop or event-less input no longer writes the parent's sentinel. Top-level sessions, including `claude --agent`, are monitored as before. (#6360) (#6365)
- **The isolation guard no longer tells the orchestrator to add the harness flag when a recorded degrade refused it** — a flag-less executor dispatch blocked after a base-check or recorded `none` degrade was told to add `isolation="worktree"`, the very action the degrade had refused; the deny now names the recorded degrade and how to record a decision for the dispatch, for the Claude guard and the Cursor hook alike, while the block decision and reason code are unchanged. (#6028) (#6371)
- **The code-review disposition ledger no longer ignores fix-report findings under other section titles** — a fix report that titled its sections `## Fixed` and `## Skipped` (or anything but the two template titles) left every fixed finding `open` with no note. `## Fixed` and `## Skipped` now classify like `## Fixed Issues` and `## Skipped Issues`, and any finding heading left under a section the step does not recognise is named on the verdict line with its report file. (#6126) (#6411)
- **`state update-progress` and `state sync` name the cause and the fix when they decline as unscoped** — a project whose STATE.md `milestone:` names a version with no matching ROADMAP.md heading (for example a flat ROADMAP with no milestone headings) declined on every call with only `phase scope is unscoped, not complete`, so its counters drifted unnoticed; the warning and a new `hint` field (non-raw output) now name the milestone and the fix for the actual cause (set `milestone: null`, add the heading above its phases, name a milestone in STATE.md, or reword a Phase title that reads as a milestone heading). The scope classification is unchanged. (#6271) (#6472)
- **`check tdd-red-evidence` accepts a real node:test RED from `assert.throws`/`assert.rejects` with a RegExp** — node:test repeats `error` and `stack` in that test's diagnostic block; strict YAML rejected the duplicates and the whole report was refused as `invalid_record`. A diagnostic block whose only defect is repeated keys is now recovered (fail-closed: interruptions, a repeated `failureType`, any other YAML error, anchors and truncated blocks still refuse). (#5819) (#5870)
- **The model-profiles advisor section matches its upstream sources and states the caveats** — it no longer points at the closed-as-not-planned per-subagent advisor tracker as pending, gives the first release that mentions the advisor (v2.1.117) instead of a version no changelog entry supports, and now says every advisor call sends the calling agent's full transcript, that the advisor's own read is uncached by default, that advisor tokens are billed separately in `usage.iterations[]`, how to turn the advisor off, and that a subagent inherits the advisor only if it passes the same pairing check. (#6205) (#6447)
- **`/gsd-pr-branch origin/main` hands `gh` the branch name, not the remote ref** — the printed `gh pr create --base` hint and the sub-repo companion PR used the target verbatim, so a remote-qualified target produced `--base origin/main`; both now use the bare branch name derived once from the target by removing a leading configured-remote name, while git operations keep the full ref. (#5972) (#6490)
- **Non-Claude executor dispatch no longer breaks on apostrophes in the agent persona** — an apostrophe in the persona used to end the prompt early and run the rest as shell, so the orchestrator now writes the prompt with its file tool to a file in the `.claude` directory that the first block creates, and a second block reads it back and the prompt reaches the executor as written, trailing newlines included. The orchestrator now substitutes every plan placeholder that the blocks and the template use, and fills the template's TDD line from the `TDD_APPLICABLE=` value block 1 prints. A prompt holding a NUL byte halts instead, and every halt this adds exits 69. A prompt file a crashed wave left behind is swept after a day. (#5531) (#5617)
- **A `gaps_found` verification report whose covered files changed now reads `stale`** — `query verification status` returned `gaps_found` before the covered-fingerprint check ran, so a gap closed outside a gap-closure plan never reported stale: it kept routing to `plan-phase --gaps`, and `execute-phase` with every plan summarized exited without re-running the verifier; a `gaps_found` report with a moved fingerprint now reads `stale` (naming the moved files) and routes to the verifier re-run, while a matching fingerprint, a malformed one, or no fingerprint keeps `gaps_found`. (#6078) (#6381)
- **A checkpoint continuation in `harness-worktree` mode keeps the paused plan's commits** — the fresh isolated agent forked from the orchestrator HEAD and could not see its own plan's finished tasks, which sit on the paused executor's unmerged branch. The workflow now resumes the paused executor by its recorded agent id while its worktree exists, and otherwise passes `<paused_branch>` so the continuation fast-forwards onto it before verifying the previous commits. (#6118) (#6402)
- **Clearing the chaining flag no longer modifies a committed `.planning/config.json` that lacks it** — every plan-phase, execute-phase and transition run clears `workflow._auto_chain_active`, and in a project created without `--auto` that wrote the key (`false`, which absent already means) and left the tracked config dirty. `config-set workflow._auto_chain_active false` now leaves the file untouched when the key is absent; clearing a stale `true`, setting `true`, and every other `config-set` still write. (#6124) (#6407)
- **`/gsd-phase --insert` passes the phase you typed to `init.phase-op` and `phase.insert`** — the insert-phase workflow handed both verbs unset variables, so the context step searched for an empty phase and reported it as not found, and the insertion call received an empty after-phase and description; both fences now take the after-phase and description from one split of the typed arguments (skipping `--ws` and other flags, and stripping quotes from the after-phase). (#5961) (#6485)
- **The real-loader plugin test no longer starts `claude -p` with the developer's credentials** — it inherited `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN`, `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` and the provider-selection variables, so a contributor with one set ran a real model turn on their account, and the plugin's SessionStart hook spawned the update worker, which queried the npm registry; the spawn now carries none of them, runs with npm offline and hooks disabled, and still reads the loader's `system init` slash-command list. (#6091) (#6387)
- **`phases clear` messages and the CLI reference say the phase directories are archived, not deleted** — the `--confirm` gate and the uncommitted-changes guard told operators the command would "delete" or "permanently delete" phase directories, and the CLI reference said `--force` deletes, when the command only ever moves them into `milestones/<version>-phases/`; the guard now says `--force` archives uncommitted edits with the directory. (#5270) (#6459)
- **Headless MemPalace capture no longer starts a daemon that blocks the MCP write tools** — the capture ran `mempalace mine --daemon --background` unconditionally, and on MemPalace 3.12 `--daemon` auto-starts a daemon that holds the palace writer lock until someone runs `mempalace daemon stop`, so every MCP write tool was refused after the first headless capture; the daemon route is now used only when `mempalace daemon status` reports a running daemon, otherwise a plain `mine` is retried with bounded backoff and a final failure prints `MemPalace capture skipped — palace locked`. (#6266) (#6470)
- **A quoted `--ws` value selects its workstream** — `--ws "feature"` and `--ws 'feature'` were ignored by the workstream parse every workflow copies, so the command ran in the active workstream with no message; one pair of quotes around the name is now read like the bare name, and the lines that strip `--ws` from the remaining arguments remove the quoted form too. (#6218) (#6449)
- **Optional flags in the code-review, codebase-map, reviewer-instance and cross-runtime workflow blocks now reach the CLI under zsh** — `--since`, `--files`, `--agent` and `--executor-runtime` were passed as one joined expansion that zsh treats as a single argument, so the option was silently dropped (the code-review scope ignored the last-review commit, the codebase map was stamped without its files, the reviewer instance ran without its agent); each is now two conditional expansions, and a scan fails any new joined flag. (#6048) (#6376)
- **The orphan worktree reaper finds the directories git has forgotten** — `worktree.reap-orphans` listed candidates only from `.git/worktrees/`, so the residue a failed harness teardown leaves (an `agent-a<hex>` directory under `.claude/worktrees/` with no `.git` file and no admin entry, a full `node_modules` inside) was invisible and the verb reported `ok: true, reaped: 0`; a second pass now removes such a directory only on the positive evidence ADR-5812 requires (a harness name and branch, unregistered, no tracked file or nested repository, nothing recent, nothing git lacks, no ignored secret or user-data file the harness did not copy) by renaming it to a reserved name and deleting it without following links, and the verb output carries `scan` so `reaped: 0` from a pass that did not look is no longer an all-clear. (#4941) (#6457)
- **`roadmap validate` and `roadmap update-plan-progress` no longer let a deleted PLAN file hide behind its ROADMAP row** — deleting a plan after planning left `validate` silent and left `update-plan-progress` rewriting the `Plans:` count from disk while keeping the missing plan's row, so the count and the list disagreed with no verb to fix it; `validate` now warns (V006) about a plan row with no PLAN file and (V007) about a live PLAN file with no row in a phase that lists its plans, and `update-plan-progress` drops the rows whose file is gone (a row that wraps onto a continuation line is kept and reported). (#6270) (#6515)
- **The phase evaluation scope reads the task rows gsd-executor writes for TDD tasks, and names a SUMMARY it could not read** — a `**Task 1 (tracer):**` or `**Task 1 RED:**` row and the RED and GREEN commits listed as sub-bullets under a task row now count as task commits, so their files are in the scope instead of vanishing; and a SUMMARY whose `## Task Commits` section yields no commit id is reported in the new `unparsedSummaries` field and printed by the code-review step, rather than leaving a `resolved` scope that reads as complete. (#6215) (#6448)
- **Evaluation-scope resolution no longer fails when a root file is named like a commit id** — the resolver's `log` and `rev-list` calls that take commit ids now end them with `--`, so a repository-root file named like a task commit's sha is no longer read as a path (git exit 128), and every gate that shares the scope resolves instead of reporting it unresolvable. (#6179) (#6444)
- **Installing a capability from a Git source no longer leaves its scratch clone behind silently when removing it fails once** — the clone's temporary directory was removed in a single `rmSync` attempt whose failure was swallowed, so a writer still under it (a detached `git gc --auto`, an external scanner: `ENOTEMPTY`, `EBUSY`) left the clone on disk with nothing reported. Git is now told not to start automatic maintenance in the throwaway clone, the removal retries the way the clone's `.git` removal in the same function does, and a removal that still fails emits a `GSD_SCRATCH_CLONE_LEFT` warning naming the directory. (#6441) (#6443)
- **The secret-read guard denies a secret read that `cat` prints from a heredoc or here-string into a shell** — `cat <<'EOF' | bash` with `cat .env` in the body, `cat <<< 'cat .env' | bash`, `bash <(cat <<EOF …)` and `source <(cat <<< '…')` are scanned like the same text given to the shell directly, while the same bodies given to `wc -l` or a bare `cat` stay allowed. (#6182) (#6446)
- **The Bash secret-read guard denies `gh api -F body=@.env` and httpie `data=@.env` request items** — `gh api -F/--field key=@path` and httpie's `key=@path`, `key:=@path`, `key==@path`, `Header:@path` and `key@path` items open the named file and send its contents, but the guard only read curl's whole-word `@file` form, so each was allowed; when the resolved command is `gh api` or `http`/`https` the path after `@` is now tested, while `-f`/`--raw-field`, `@-` and commands that merely mention `http` or `gh api` stay allowed. (#5825) (#6539)
- **The Bash secret-read guard judges the operand after a lone `{` or `}`** — `cat { .env`, `cat } .env` and `grep KEY { .env` were allowed because the tokenizer took any `{` or `}` that began a word for a group separator, so the word after it was read as a new command name and never checked as a file operand; a brace now opens or closes a group only where a command may start (the start of a segment, past `then`, `do`, `else`, `!`, redirections and assignments, after an `if`/`while`/`until` condition or a `function`, `coproc`, `time`, `for`, `repeat`, `select` or `always` head, or a closer such as `esac`, which zsh also gives a `{` body), and is an ordinary word among a command's arguments, as bash, dash and zsh read it; a `}` that closes an open group is always a separator (zsh closes `{ echo x } always { … }` there); anything unclear stays a group. Real groups such as `{ cat .env; }` and a brace heredoc tag are scanned as before. (#6438) (#6543)
- **The Bash secret-read guard reads the body of a heredoc opened in a `$( )` that closed on its line as data** — `echo $(cat <<EOF) x` followed by a body line with a lone quote and then `cat .env` was allowed, because the span reader dropped the heredoc still waiting for its body and the top-level tokenizer read the body as shell, where the quote swallowed the read; the waiting heredoc now goes to the tokenizer's pending list (also from `<( )`, a double-quoted `$( )`, and across a line continuation), so its body is consumed where bash reads it and the read after it is denied. (#5515) (#6548)
- **The Bash secret-read guard reads the default of a `${…}` word as a name the command can read** — `cat ${x:-$'.env'}`, `cat ${x-$'.e\x6ev'}`, `cat ${x:+a}$'.env'` and (zsh) `cat .env${}` were allowed because the text inside `${…}` was never scanned, although the shell runs `cat .env`; a word holding `${name<op>WORD}` (`-`, `:-`, `=`, `:=`, `?`, `:?`, `+`, `:+`) or an empty `${}` is now also judged with each expansion replaced by its quote-removed WORD and by nothing, since the variable is unknown. (#6132) (#6553)
- **The Bash secret-read guard finds the command after `watch -q N`, reads `\"` in a backtick inside double quotes, and reads what a here-string or heredoc feeds `xargs`** — `watch -x -q 2 sh -c 'cat .env'` was allowed because the guard took only `-n` for an option with a separate value, so `-q`/`--equexit` shifted where it believed the watched command started (`watch` now takes its value-taking options from a table, resolves getopt's unambiguous abbreviations such as `--int` and `--equ`, and stops at `-d`, whose optional value is attached); ``echo "`cat \".env\"`"`` was allowed because a backtick inside double quotes kept the backslash before `"` that the shell removes, so the scanned text was not the text the shell runs (a backtick in a heredoc body, in `$(( ))` inside double quotes, or seen outside quotes is scanned both ways, since dash and zsh unescape and bash does not, so ``echo `cat \".env\"` `` for a file literally named with quotes is now denied too); and `xargs cat <<< .env` or `xargs cat <<EOF` with `.env` in the body was allowed because only a pipe was read as the names `xargs` receives. (#6433) (#6550)
- **A capability contribution declared `into: verifier` now reaches the verifier** — it installed and showed in the rendered hooks but was dropped silently, including MemPalace's problem-capture instructions; contributions declared at `execute:post` now go into the verifier's prompt, and MemPalace's moved there from `execute:wave:post`, where no verifier runs. (#5984) (#6349)
- **The executor's TDD gate-commit lookups accept a breaking-change `!` subject** — a `feat(01-03)!:` or `test(01-03)!:` plan commit counts in the TDD review checkpoint, but the RED, GREEN and REFACTOR lookups in the TDD reference anchored on `):` and missed it, so the executor wrote a false violation under `## TDD Gate Compliance`. The three lookups now accept the optional `!`. (#6120) (#6404)
- **The secret-read guard now denies reads hidden in strings that `find`, `xargs` and `watch` re-interpret** — `find -exec sh -c 'cat .env'`, a shell behind a wrapper under `xargs` (`xargs sudo|timeout|env sh -c '…'`), a quoted word such as `@".env"` piped into `xargs` (which removes the quotes before the sub-command sees it), and `watch` (which joins its operands and runs them through `sh -c`) were allowed while `cat .env` was denied; each is now read as the command it becomes, the plain forms stay denied, and non-secret names near the same constructs stay allowed. (#6114) (#6397)
- **Five timeout tests no longer leave their stalling `sleep` running after they pass** — the test fixtures planted `sleep N` under a shell (or under `git`), so the timeout killed the shell and the `sleep` was reparented and ran out its 1 to 12 seconds; each stall is now `exec`'d so the killed process is the stall, the git-hook test terminates the hook-started stalls itself, and each test asserts nothing it started is still running (on POSIX hosts, where `ps` can check it). (#6086) (#6382)
- **The executor stall check now sees a worktree executor's commits before the wave merges** — with `isolation="worktree"` an executor commits to its own unmerged agent branch and writes its SUMMARY there, so the `${EXPECTED_BRANCH}` probe read no progress and the pause (`continue waiting` / `kill and retry` / `kill and switch to inline execution`) fired for an executor that was committing normally; the stall surveillance now asks the evaluation-scope resolver for the plan's commits since dispatch across every local branch (a new opt-in `check evaluation-scope --all-branches`, plan and quick units only, which reports `latestCommitTime`) and a commit resets the no-progress clock, while sequential mode keeps its probe, the gates keep their reachable-from-ref contract, and an executor with no commits and no SUMMARY past the threshold still reaches the pause. (#6117) (#6400)
- **`execute-phase` always resumes at the verification gates for a stale report when every plan is summarized** — the all-plans-summarized branch was prose the orchestrating model had to evaluate, so a stale `passed` report could be read as "already complete" and the verifier skipped on a judgment that the change was test-only; a new `verification all-summarized` query computes the decision (exit, present the owner's route, update the roadmap, or resume at the gates) from the same routing table as `verification status`, and the workflow branches on its output. (#6096) (#6391)
- **`/gsd-next` and `/gsd-progress --next` route to `/gsd-resume-work` after a pause** — `/gsd-pause-work` writes `.planning/HANDOFF.json` but never `paused_at`, so the smart-entry "paused" situation and the next workflow's Route 8 could not fire after a pause, and `--next` hard-stopped only for a root-level `.continue-here.md`, not the phase-scoped one pause-work usually writes; the handoff file now classifies as paused (and `/gsd-resume-work` deleting it routes forward again), and a new Gate 0 in the next workflow routes a recorded pause to resume before any other gate. (#6431) (#6477)
- **execute-phase records phase start in STATE.md** — the begin-phase block passed `--phase`, `--name` and `--plans` variables that no step set for it (each workflow fence is its own shell), so `state begin-phase` exited with `Invalid --plans value` and STATE.md never recorded the active phase; the block now assigns the phase number placeholder, reads the curated name from `roadmap.get-phase` and the plan count from `find-phase` (both workstream-scoped), and stops when the plan count cannot be read. (#6258) (#6469)
- **A plain `query dispatch-isolation` re-query no longer clobbers a degrade that mandated sequential execution, so the isolation guard stops denying the dispatch the degrade itself asked for** — the #683 worktree base-check degrade is now re-derived by the resolver on every unheld call that carries no `--plan`, as the `use_worktrees` opt-out has been since #3737, so a repo whose HEAD has diverged from its fork base keeps recording `none` across later plain queries that carry no `--plan` (#4222); and a `none` that a dispatch site records with `--force-isolation none`, which the resolver cannot re-derive, is held by a later plain query in its scope while it is fresh (#4561). (#4904) (#6494)
- **The TDD gate finds a RED commit made of capitalised test files** — the task router already treated `Tests/foo.rs`, `Foo.TEST.js` and `Foo_Test.go` as test files, but the gate's RED-commit search used plain git pathspecs, which are case-sensitive, so a RED commit touching only such files was invisible and the gate reported a missing RED commit; the gate now passes the same shared list behind git's `:(icase)` magic, so router and gate agree on letter case for the paths the gate already matches, and lowercase layouts behave as before. (#5766) (#6528)
- **The ship-a-reviewer-lane how-to names the approved-issue step for registry PRs** — the page told an author to append a registry entry and open a PR without saying the PR needs a linked issue with a maintainer-applied approval label, so a contributor following only that page had the PR auto-closed; it now states the step and links the Submission process, and the registry-docs parity guard covers the page. (#6109) (#6468)
- **The docs-update doc verifier now runs on its resolved model** — `/gsd:docs-update` resolved a model for `gsd-doc-verifier` but never passed it to any of its three verifier spawns, so project `model_profile` and overrides had no effect on the verifier; a new guard fails any workflow that resolves a model it never passes to a spawn. (#5997) (#6366)
- **A `fix(<phase>-<plan>)` GREEN commit no longer hard-stops `verify-phase-goal`** — under `tdd_mode`, `tdd.review-checkpoint` reported a plan whose GREEN commit was `fix(<phase>-<plan>)` as missing GREEN; the gate now accepts `feat` or `fix`, and the TDD reference, planner, and executor docs state the same rule. The `Expected commit pattern:` and `GREEN precedes RED` lines of the `tdd.review-checkpoint` output now name `fix(...)` beside `feat(...)`, and the executor halt reason `feat_before_test` is renamed `impl_before_test`; scripts that match the old halt-reason token or the old hint text must change. (#5274) (#5455)
- **`--pick` works on `extract-messages` and `profile-sample`, and a large `profile-sample` result is printed as JSON** — `gsd-tools extract-messages <project> --pick messages_extracted` and `gsd-tools profile-sample --pick messages_sampled` failed with "command output was not JSON" and exit code 1, and a `profile-sample` result over 50 KB was printed as a bare `@file:<path>` line instead of the JSON it names. Both commands now go through the same output handling as every other command. (#6332) (#6359)
- **The eval-review, execute-plan and AI-integration workflows now omit a blank or `inherit` model instead of passing it to the agent spawn** — on runtimes without native tier aliases the spawn failed, and the AI-integration phase never passed its four resolved models at all, so model profile and overrides had no effect there; the #2517 guard also now sees prose and unquoted spawns so no new site escapes it. (#5996) (#6363)

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/open-gsd/gsd-core/compare/v1.22.0...v1.23.0

name: v19.1.1
body:
## @oh-my-pi/pi-agent-core

### Fixed

- Prevented oversized handoffs from reaching the provider by detecting when prepared context exceeds the target model’s context window.
- Preserved provider error status, error identifiers, retry classification, and cancellation markers on failed or cancelled assistant turns.
- Fixed speculative tool calls hanging when discarded or aborted before execution completed.

## @oh-my-pi/pi-ai

### Added

- Added `AssistantMessage.requestId`, populated from Anthropic’s `request-id` response header, so failed or refused requests retain the identifier needed for Anthropic support.
- Added `GET /v1/pi/models` to `omp auth-gateway`, serving the gateway's model catalog (limits, thinking levels, pricing) to pi-native clients.

### Changed

- Devin account selection now prioritizes logins with remaining daily or weekly quota, then accounts funded by on-demand balance, while skipping accounts with no available capacity. Devin logins also track email, user ID, and organization so separate organizations are distinguishable in `omp usage` and `auth.accountPolicies`; existing logins must be reauthenticated to populate this information.
- Billing failures from providers are now treated as usage limits, allowing retries to rotate accounts and continue through the model fallback chain.
- Provider usage reports registered by extensions now persist across omp processes, avoiding unnecessary repeated usage-endpoint checks.
- Requests that stall during provider operations are now classified as timeouts, allowing automatic fallback to another model.
- Reduced idle memory usage by loading prompt-perturbation data only when perturbation is enabled for a request.

### Fixed

- Fixed split tool-call handling so models configured with `splitToolCalls` receive each tool call together with its corresponding result in the correct message order.
- Fixed `apple/on-device` finish-reason handling so requests no longer emit spurious stderr warnings and correctly report recognized stop or length completions.
- Improved local validation for empty Anthropic requests by reporting the model, provider, and received message count instead of an opaque provider error.
- Fixed OpenAI and Codex requests failing on MCP tool schemas containing unsupported unescaped character patterns.
- OpenRouter Responses requests that end in an unbilled encrypted reasoning item now surface the underlying provider failure instead of completing silently.
- Fixed preservation of Gemini thought signatures across tool calls when using Portkey or the authentication gateway.
- Fixed the thinking-loop guard incorrectly retrying final answers containing long Markdown tables or similarly shaped JSON records.
- Fixed strict tool-schema conversion so object properties that accept arbitrary fields are not incorrectly restricted to empty objects.
- Fixed `antigravity-cli` models failing to receive images returned by tools such as `read`.
- Fixed transient proxy errors from disrupting snapshot streaming and disabling usage reporting for the remainder of the process.
- Fixed concurrent Antigravity CLI sessions for the same account failing during credential staging.
- Fixed OpenAI Codex WebSocket continuations so sticky turn routing information is preserved for subsequent requests.
- Improved recovery from a corrupt `agent.db` so readable provider credentials are restored where possible and disabled credentials remain disabled.

## @oh-my-pi/browser-relay

### Fixed

- The side panel’s Connection settings now show the browser’s specific reason when it refuses the native host (for example, because native messaging is blocked by enterprise policy), instead of incorrectly suggesting that the host may be missing.

## @oh-my-pi/pi-catalog

### Added

- Z.AI (`zai`) now discovers the models available to your GLM Coding Plan key, so newly released GLM models appear without waiting for a catalog update.
- Added `getUpstreamPin()` and `routedModelsAreEqual()` to `@oh-my-pi/pi-catalog/models` for distinguishing aggregator models routed to different upstream providers.
- Added `@oh-my-pi/pi-catalog/discovery/pi-native` and `piNativeModelManagerOptions()` for reading a provider's model roster from an auth gateway's `GET /v1/pi/models`.

### Fixed

- Fixed Llama 3.x models failing after turns that invoked multiple tools when served through vLLM-based hosts, including CoreWeave through OpenRouter.
- Devin usage is now kept separate for organizations that share the same email address.
- Updated Devin image token accounting to match Devin’s published 1,089-token charge per image across supported Gemini image models.
- Corrected Devin pricing and context limits for GPT-5.6 Sol, Terra, and Luna Fast lanes, including long-context rates above 272K input tokens and the standard 272K limit when Extended Context is disabled.
- Corrected Cursor pricing for GPT-5.6 Sol, Terra, and Luna models so output above 272K input tokens uses the documented 1.5× rate.
- Turning thinking off for GPT-6.1 Terra now uses the supported `none` reasoning effort.
- Fixed GPT-6.2 and later OpenAI Responses models losing reasoning context after session pruning and subsequent tool calls.
- Corrected Bedrock Kimi K3.1 Pro Highspeed reasoning options and effort handling.
- GitHub Copilot now lists only models available to the account, including after restarting.
- Codex models discovered before being bundled now use their formatted display names, such as `GPT-6.2 Sol`.

## @oh-my-pi/pi-coding-agent

### Breaking Changes

- The native shell Rust API now stores indexed variables as `IndexedArray` instead of `Vec`; construct `VarValue::Indexed` values with `items.into()`.

### Added

- Added the opt-in `tree` status segment, which shows a session’s position in the session tree after a rewind or on a branch; in Tern, the segment opens `/tree` when clicked.
- Providers routed through an auth gateway (`transport: pi-native`) now list the gateway's models, so models the gateway discovered at runtime (such as new Codex models) can be selected without declaring them in `models.yml`, and models the gateway cannot route are hidden.
- Added `computer.takeover` as the replacement for `computer.backgroundFallback`, with `fallback`, `foreground`, and `always` modes for controlling when the computer tool takes over the foreground window. Existing fallback behavior is preserved by default.
- Added a portable `column` shell builtin with util-linux-compatible options, including table formatting, named columns, alignment, hiding, ordering, JSON output, tree display, and width controls.
- Added extension todo backends through `pi.registerTodoBackend()` and the `todo.backend` setting. Registered backends can mirror the session’s complete todo list to an external store and can be selected and configured from `/settings` → Tools → Todos.
- `/wt` now runs the new worktree’s `post-checkout` hook, displays progress in the TUI, and loads skills and commands created by the hook. Failed hooks leave the worktree intact and display a warning.

### Changed

- Empty-stop recovery now records each retry with the selected model, provider, and stop metadata, making repeated empty model responses visible in the session log.
- The quick model picker refreshes stale provider catalogs in the background, so long-running sessions can discover newly available models.
- On Linux, language-server file watching now adapts to the inotify watch limit so large workspaces are less likely to interfere with other file watchers and system services.
- The `eval` tool now documents its default 30-second cell deadline in its prompt and timeout parameter.

### Fixed

- Improved Magic Edit so it can search and read the current draft, retry failed replacements without losing successful edits, validate syntax before writing, and support models that emit tool calls as text.
- Fixed shell tool command handling when `bash` is replaced by an extension, including support for tool-only command lines with remote or sandboxed shells.
- Fixed browser scrolling validation and documentation so invalid object forms explain the correct pixel-delta signature and equivalent call.
- Fixed `ask` handling of fieldsets whose radio buttons use different names, preventing a preselected option from being submitted alongside the user’s choice.
- Fixed title generation to stop when a model explicitly declines with `<title/>` or `none`, while continuing to the next candidate for errors or unusable replies.
- Fixed automatic and speculative compaction so oversized or non-retriable handoff requests move on to the next available compaction method instead of being repeatedly sent to a provider.
- `wait()` in eval cells now accepts displayed subagent IDs, including the `agent://id` form, while still rejecting handles belonging to other sessions.
- Fixed startup and session model configuration so thinking levels, model-provider ordering, enabled-model allowlists, routed selections, and pinned upstream routes remain consistent across model switches, cycling, restore, plan mode, and metadata refreshes.
- Fixed queued follow-up messages being lost when interrupted responses are discarded, and fixed TTSR interruptions that could leave a session unable to continue.
- Fixed OpenAI Responses sessions rewriting previously sent tool results, which could cause later reasoning items to be rejected.
- Fixed format-on-write and symlink-related file editing issues, including incorrect write failures, missing snapshots, duplicated `local://` paths, and incorrect symlinked filenames in previews and journals.
- Fixed Windows browser downloads occasionally retaining temporary GUID filenames when the downloaded file was briefly locked.
- Fixed RPC shutdown leaving MCP subprocesses running after the session ended.
- Fixed advisor and Spotlight output so truncated or repeated tool results are represented accurately without losing the original content.
- Fixed first-run startup warnings that persisted after a default model had been selected.
- Fixed context rollover handling so concurrent bookkeeping no longer silently drops an explicit rollover, and skipped rollovers produce a warning.
- `/omfg` now closes its panel after successfully saving a rule and shows the saved path; errors keep the panel open.
- Fixed shell handling of leading `cd` commands that use glob, brace, or named-user home expansion.
- Claude-format plugin agents now correctly map Claude tool names such as `WebFetch`, `WebSearch`, `TodoWrite`, `AskUserQuestion`, `MultiEdit`, and `Agent` to their OMP equivalents.
- Startup extension notifications now remain visible instead of being overwritten by later notices or MCP startup status.
- Fixed CLI parsing so `--plan` no longer consumes a following CLI flag as its value during startup, restart, fork, or subcommand routing.
- Fixed `/usage` when the usage database is temporarily locked; stored history remains visible and is marked unsynced if it cannot be refreshed.
- Model discovery now classifies speech-only and transcription-only models as TTS and STT models rather than chat models.
- Subagents stopped by their parent now record that they were stopped by the parent agent.
- Fixed SDK and extension imports, examples, and session-specific extension discovery for RPC and ACP sessions.
- Fixed X and YouTube URL reads to honor SDK session settings even when global settings have not been initialized.
- Restored sessions now correctly report background jobs whose outcome is unknown, and `omp --restore` no longer replays completed turns after idle compaction or interruption.
- Selective commits now preserve the drafted contents and Git clean-filter results for binary, non-text, oversized, and Git LFS files, and avoid overwriting files changed since the draft was created.
- Fixed `read` hanging on images and other non-text files when speculative execution and `beforeToolCall` hooks are enabled.
- Provider error logs now include the request ID needed for troubleshooting Anthropic refusals.
- Sessions started from collaboration prompts now receive automatic titles.
- Fixed `/tan` forks ending an idle wait prematurely when their assignment remains blocked.

## @oh-my-pi/pi-natives

### Fixed

- Fixed `grep()`, `glob()`, `fuzzyFind()`, `astGrep()`, `astEdit()`, and recursive shell search commands occasionally hanging on machines with many CPUs.
- Fixed cancellation and timeout races in native search, file-matching, fuzzy-search, AST, and editing operations that could cause crashes or use-after-free errors.
- Fixed `grep()` with a match limit reporting incomplete results instead of rejecting when its directory walk failed.
- Fixed `@oh-my-pi/pi-natives` failing to load when installed from Bun's cache or when standalone binaries had extracted native addons from another build.
- Fixed Linux Wayland accessibility and automation support for GTK dialogs, control values, and selected rows, list items, and tabs.
- Fixed Linux PTY output occasionally including an extra blank line after a command exits.
- Fixed keypad navigation keys being dropped when NumLock is off under the kitty keyboard protocol.
- Fixed Wayland screenshots incorrectly timing out while waiting for the screen-share picker.
- Improved Windows accessibility action reliability by reporting uncertain dispatches accurately and preventing actions from being sent after their reply wait has expired.
- Fixed Windows automation of classic Win32 and WinForms buttons and checkboxes incorrectly activating the application or reporting success without performing the click.
- Fixed macOS computer-control takeover restoration so the previously active window is restored correctly after automation ends, with failures reported when restoration cannot be confirmed.
- Fixed macOS background keyboard and scroll events, including events sent through iPhone Mirroring, being lost or unexpectedly activating another window.
- Fixed X11 typing of non-Latin and other characters outside the active keyboard layout.
- Binary patches now refuse to apply when the target file does not match the version the patch was created from, preventing accidental replacement of changed files.
- On Windows, aborting or timing out an in-process utility blocked on an open empty stdin pipe now terminates it without waiting for the pipe writer.

### Removed

- Removed the startup warning shown when a source checkout loads a native addon from another release; incompatible addons still produce an actionable error when a required symbol is unavailable.

## @oh-my-pi/snapcompact

### Fixed

- Fixed snapcompact archive summaries so they accurately report the grid layout of dense middle frames.

## @oh-my-pi/omp-stats

### Added

- Added `readDailyActivity()` for reading stored daily activity without being blocked by another process writing to the stats database; it returns `null` when no stats database exists.

### Fixed

- Fixed Spotlight baseline and adjusted-net calculations to use consistent result sets, improving headline and step-row accuracy.

## @oh-my-pi/pi-tui

### Added

- Added host-provided runtime choices for settings menus through `SettingsRuntimeContext.runtimeOptions`, while preserving built-in choices for thinking levels, themes, and composer shapes.
- Added interrupt metadata so hosts can distinguish a parent-agent termination from a user-initiated interrupt.

### Fixed

- Fixed handoffs being skipped when only the model’s upstream pin changes.
- Fixed the `/usage` activity calendar retaining its history when a refresh fails, while indicating that the data is not synced.
- Fixed SVG images blinking in ask forms when questions extend beyond the panel.
- Fixed the active-turn status line so elapsed time updates smoothly at tenths of a second.
- Fixed assigning a model to a role when pressing Enter again on the selected model, which could incorrectly remove the role.
- Updated the quick model picker (`Alt+P`) to include models added to the catalog after a session began, even when the session is restricted by `--models` or `enabledModels`.
- Fixed images and other path-based files appearing as unavailable in Tern when the TUI and Tern run on different machines or in local sessions without Tern’s shared file directory.

### Removed

- Removed `OmfgPanelComponent.markSaved` and the `saved` panel state; the `/omfg` panel now closes after a rule is saved.

name: v4.23.1
body:
[![Tokscale](https://github.com/junhoyeo/tokscale/raw/main/.github/assets/hero-v3.png)](https://github.com/junhoyeo/tokscale) # `tokscale@v4.23.1` is here!
- Price gpt-6.2 Astra and Sol requests above 272k input tokens at the long-context rate for the whole request. - Count Zed threads that run on a ChatGPT subscription. - Show saved Pi session names in the Sessions view. - Report an unreadable Claude Keychain item in the Usage view instead of hiding Claude. - Recover Kimi Code response timing from native step events. - Fix autosubmit skipping every other scheduled run. - Count every registered client in `tokscale wrapped` when no client flag is set. ## What's Changed * fix(pricing): apply full-request 272k pricing to gpt-6.2 models by @Kanggod9 in https://github.com/junhoyeo/tokscale/pull/1657 * fix(pi): display saved session names by @The-Minion-oOo in https://github.com/junhoyeo/tokscale/pull/1656 * fix(zed): count native ChatGPT subscription sessions by @The-Minion-oOo in https://github.com/junhoyeo/tokscale/pull/1655 * fix(usage): surface unreadable Claude Keychain credentials instead of hiding Claude by @raw34 in https://github.com/junhoyeo/tokscale/pull/1654 * fix(kimi): recover response timing from native step events by @yoloytz in https://github.com/junhoyeo/tokscale/pull/1644 * fix(autosubmit): stop skipping every other scheduled run by @Emirfs in https://github.com/junhoyeo/tokscale/pull/1650 * fix(wrapped): count every registered client when no client flag is set by @ruanchaves in https://github.com/junhoyeo/tokscale/pull/1645 ## New Contributors * @Kanggod9 made their first contribution in https://github.com/junhoyeo/tokscale/pull/1657 * @yoloytz made their first contribution in https://github.com/junhoyeo/tokscale/pull/1644 * @Emirfs made their first contribution in https://github.com/junhoyeo/tokscale/pull/1650 * @ruanchaves made their first contribution in https://github.com/junhoyeo/tokscale/pull/1645 **Full Changelog**: https://github.com/junhoyeo/tokscale/compare/v4.23.0...v4.23.1

**Highlights**

- Faster app launch and dubbing start, and installers about 425 MB smaller (#4320, #4322, #4323)
- Generate and the MCP tool add paragraph pauses and understand [slow], [fast], [emphasis] and [spell] (#4254)
- Dubbing no longer renders an untranslated track as the target language, and a finished dub always exports (#4347, #4346)
- Linux ROCm dictation stays on the GPU, including 4 GB AMD cards (#4327, #4336)
- OmniVoice frees its GPU memory on unload and always loads its reviewed model version (#4355, #4360)

### Changed

- The Dub demo videos now download on demand (about 10 MB, only when you click Download) instead of shipping inside the app (#4326)

- Windows, macOS and Linux installers drop about 425 MB of unused UI packages from the app archive (#4322)

- Faster Electron app launch, UI navigation, and backend engine/database startup across macOS, Windows, and Linux (#4320)
- The title bar offers "Get Pro app" to Pro accounts, linking to the Pro download in your dashboard, and "Upgrade to Pro" to other signed-in accounts (#4287) — thanks @micronox for the report

- Removed the unused retired desktop release cleanup helper and its ownership entry. (#4172) — thanks @salemalkadadi-debug!
- Removed an unused legacy update-busy helper while retaining active restart protection (#4149) — thanks @themrbeasley!
- Retired an unused legacy update toast while preserving the active Electron update controls (#4141) — thanks @themrbeasley!

body:
## 2026.11.10-beta.2

### Highlights

- Update recovery: keep OpenClaw runnable when package replacement is interrupted, and let the next update finish safely after a crash or reboot. (#200273, #200366, #200460, #200550, #200994) Thanks @fuller-stack-dev.
- Reliable background work: preserve finished subagent results and resume their delivery after Gateway restarts, interrupted parent turns, and sibling activity. (#200279, #200649, #200249, #201544, #201563) Authored by @steipete. Thanks @RomneyDa, @vincentkoc, and @obviyus.
- Faster first conversations: accept the first chat while model catalogs load, keep readiness checks responsive, and compact long histories without holding them entirely in Gateway memory. (#201127, #200370, #201304) Related #195361 Authored by @steipete. Thanks @RomneyDa, @jalehman, and @garrytan.

### Changes

- Agent templates: open a durable chat before verified setup finishes, while retaining rollback authorization for newly created agents. (#196392, #200300) Related #196048 Thanks @Patrick-Erichsen and @anmol0b.
- Plugin side questions: let plugins fork a session’s live context for background work with their own tools and policy-controlled file and command access. (#170146, #190950, #200636) Thanks @obviyus.
- Webhooks: accept bodies up to 1 MiB, report rejected requests, and fan out batched Gmail notifications. (#200514, #130002) Authored by @steipete. Thanks @garrytan and @obviyus.

### Fixes

- Secret-backed skill keys: preserve SecretRef values when keys are edited through the Skills page or skills.update instead of replacing references with plaintext. (#200539, #197319) Related #193149 Thanks @obviyus, @tommyjoseph, and @mmaps.
- Permission boundaries: retain the admitted requester’s authority across restart recovery and native UI clients, and keep queued input from ending without a recorded cause. (#200394, #181363, #194443, #200433) Authored by @steipete. Thanks @RomneyDa, @vincentkoc, @jjjhenriksen, @sallyom, @VACInc, and @obviyus.
- Chat delivery: finish replies interrupted by Gateway restarts, preserve channel message IDs on oversized history entries, and reject stale-pane sends after a conversation branch switches. (#200553, #201698, #113073) Authored by @steipete. Thanks @vincentkoc, @RomneyDa, and @obviyus.
- Subagent conversations: deliver completed results while siblings are still running or waiting, preserve each result under its requester turn, and stop sessions_send from blocking beyond its timeout. (#190999, #200967, #200873, #201373) Related #188422 Authored by @steipete. Thanks @vincentkoc, @RomneyDa, @gouyu-hou, @obviyus, and @esqandil.
- Live steering: deliver new instructions to busy subagents immediately, keep background turns running through configuration edits, and allow steering while a Code Mode command is active. (#200574, #200516, #200998) Thanks @obviyus, @RomneyDa, and @VACInc.
- Automation continuity: retain scheduled work when chats, groups, or sharing change, preserve owner/account bindings across handoffs, and keep carried-over jobs running after updates. (#200314, #200396, #201434, #201008, #200653) Related #200307, #200600 Thanks @RomneyDa, @vincentkoc, @hannesrudolph, @obviyus, @daniel-lxs, and @VACInc.
- Automation outcomes: distinguish recovered tool errors, genuine tool failures, and successfully delivered reports; suppress notices for expected skips rather than reporting them as failed starts. (#201638, #107735, #139037, #120056, #152165, #186652, #194276, #200032) Related #102206, #116731, #194261, #200030 Authored by @steipete. Thanks @obviyus, @joshavant, @solavrc, @hartmark, @NarahariRaghava, @warren2008-2020-spec, @pash-openai, @wr-web, @slatem, and @daniel-lxs.
- Telegram: keep receiving messages when update IDs restart, and answer messages even when an attachment cannot be downloaded. (#201167, #200682) Thanks @RomneyDa and @obviyus.
- Discord and WhatsApp: reconnect all Discord accounts after network outages, preserve independent requests instead of replacing active tasks, and avoid flooding sessions with WhatsApp reconnect notices. (#201415, #201518, #191037) Related #162189, #190640 Thanks @RomneyDa, @vincentkoc, @obviyus, @mattreyes0824, @ericcurtin, and @sercada.
- Matrix and Slack: prevent quoted bot mentions from starting new Matrix turns, render Matrix polls and votes in Element X, and retain Slack questions when an unauthorized person presses a button. (#197091, #191700, #201371) Related #197065, #191678, #201348 Thanks @Jo2234, @obviyus, @chelsealong, @geekforlife, and @shannon0430.
- Media and meetings: expose inbound Twilio MMS photos to agents, retain long Feishu streaming replies, and keep meeting audio and captions alive after a join request returns. (#200890, #161777, #191059, #178415) Related #200804, #139443, #173896, #178413 Thanks @deepujain, @obviyus, @potterdigital, @ArthurNie, @Simon2256928, @valkyriweb, @jeremynorris, and @sukhdeepjohar.
- Talk and mobile: load conversation history for fresh calls, keep iOS spoken replies beside the turn that prompted them, and avoid stale roles in approval alerts. (#201352, #197136, #200360) Related #197129 Thanks @davelutztx, @xena68, @obviyus, @Marvinthebored, @Peetiegonzalez, @vyctorbrzezowski, and @joshavant.
- Claude CLI: retain final answers after progress and large tool results, avoid redoing completed tool work on fallback, and preserve long child results in completion turns. (#200501, #166127, #200801, #200470, #200226) Related #186967, #200744, #199633 Thanks @RomneyDa, @vincentkoc, @obviyus, @Trinity-AI-Coder, @RTapiador, @fede-kamel, @jzmudzinski, @chaeyn, @etzelm, @VACInc, and @mulderp82.
- Codex conversations: preserve instructions and oversized request content, recover media-only turns, avoid MCP name collisions, and retain line breaks in streamed replies. (#200690, #200735, #185186, #194831, #201102) Related #185079, #194825 Thanks @RomneyDa, @vincentkoc, @obviyus, @kaguranananana, @UHDPass, @lonexreb, @NicoBoom13, and @freeqaz.
- Model discovery: discover new ChatGPT subscription models independently of npm releases, use published catalog limits, retain account reasoning limits, and keep healthy fallback models available. (#201130, #201493, #200403, #200446, #200946) Related #201480 Thanks @RomneyDa, @daniel-lxs, @vincentkoc, @obviyus, and @VACInc.
- Tool access: show required arguments for wide schemas and initial Knowledge tools, preserve full Tool Search pages, validate compact-tool arguments, and leave an empty tools.allow unrestricted. (#200064, #200339, #201487, #114461, #197590) Related #194857, #96115, #111704, #197552 Authored by @steipete. Thanks @jalehman, @vincentkoc, @lyrakat, @cbertucci33, @pallaoro, @wr-web, and @primepal2.
- Browser control: keep page reads attached to the correct page after navigation, preserve the user’s focused Chrome tab, and allow screenshots of background tabs in headless mode. (#196659, #134400, #201626) Related #196658 Authored by @steipete. Thanks @RomneyDa, @vincentkoc, @martins-oss, @obviyus, and @scotthuang.
- Install and update: tolerate concurrent database writers, preserve completed core updates when plugin or service refreshes need retrying, and finish when unchanged plugin configuration is read-only. (#200742, #201545, #201330, #200507, #200331, #201331) Authored by @steipete. Thanks @fuller-stack-dev.
- Older installations: bridge older updater layouts, preserve valid archives, recover interrupted source-checkout updates, and retain package installs when an old wrapper cannot be removed. (#200662, #201314, #200659, #200733, #201009, #200579) Related #200594 Authored by @steipete. Thanks @RomneyDa, @SimonAIbot, and @fuller-stack-dev.
- Linux and Windows updates: avoid RAM-backed temporary-directory exhaustion when TMPDIR is unset, accept pre-existing service drop-ins, validate staged Windows plugin dependencies, and redact Windows home paths from Doctor failure reports. (#199689, #197378, #200595, #200457) Related #197377, #200573, #200451 Authored by @steipete. Thanks @kitiyeung, @holgergruenhagen, @sallyom, @desksk, and @LolPanda2004.
- Storage recovery: preserve PostgreSQL startup and backup restore paths, allow supported moves between SQLite and PostgreSQL, and speed up network database ports. (#197425, #193596, #197795, #200383, #201299, #201374) Related #196966, #197779, #200356, #201250, #201249 Authored by @steipete. Thanks @ceckert, @VACInc, @etzelm, @chelsealong, @evemorgen, and @deepujain.
- History and responsiveness: reduce stalls in transcript searches, sparse-history reads, filesystem-heavy work, plugin reload recovery, and background page cleanup. (#200355, #201566, #200793, #197510, #200320, #200374, #201445) Authored by @steipete. Thanks @VACInc and @RomneyDa.
- Desktop startup: let the macOS app answer its first chat and reopen after credential startup failures; finish VNC authentication before readiness probes close. (#200373, #201505, #193487) Related #200340, #193444 Thanks @jalehman, @jjjhenriksen, @SebTardif, @obviyus, and @lakemike.

- Replay timestamps: preserve the original user-turn timestamp across attachment preparation and worker replay. Thanks @RomneyDa and @vincentkoc.
- Setup and authentication: discover cold account models before inference and classify model-route credential mismatches correctly. Thanks @RomneyDa, @daniel-lxs, @vincentkoc, and @DanCanadian.
- Update diagnostics: retain nested handoff failure details and distinguish snapshot capacity failures from database corruption. Thanks @qodelicious, @RomneyDa, @vincentkoc, and @machine3at.

### Complete contribution record

This audited record covers the complete v2026.11.10-beta.1..906bbc529b0bfd24a9108d124c1aeefe9acc0176 history: 356 in-range PRs + 0 retained seed-only PRs = 356 unique PRs. The generation manifest also supplies direct commits as editorial input; the grouped notes above prioritize user impact.
